mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary inflation and rate-hike signal, which increases risk-off sentiment and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.5% for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly positive at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.7% for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.7% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly positive at the 5% level.
